text: Hey, it's Sophie. Have you got a minute?
It's about the starred number Lucas brought up in the group.
I know we already talked about it, but I went through Daniel's contact export again.
There's something I missed.
I kept thinking about how that conversation ended.
Lucas was upset that I'd invited someone none of us knew,
and I couldn't really explain why your number was there.
So I went back to the file.
This time, I opened the actual contact entry instead of just looking at the list.
There's a field under the number called Remarks.
I didn't see it the first time because it only appears when you open the entry.
Most of the contacts have nothing written there.
But the starred one, it has something.
The problem is, I can't read it properly.
A few letters show up, then gaps, and these little square symbols.
It's not even a complete sentence.
I tried looking at it again, but I still can't make sense of it.
I don't want to pretend I know what it says.
The number itself is clear, though.
I checked it against the one I used to message you, and it matches.
We already knew about the star.
That's what Lucas noticed.
What's new is this damaged remark beside it.
I just don't know if the two things mean anything together.
I found this copy in the family folder Daniel shared with me,
but I don't know who originally exported it, or whether anyone changed it afterward.
The file shows some dates, but I don't know if they're from the original contacts
or just from when someone copied it.
I wish I could be more certain.
Daniel used to make little notes for everything.
Lists, reminders, even reminders to check his other reminders.
I'd tease him about it, and he'd say,
there's a system, Soph.
You just don't understand it.
I miss that.
But just because he liked making notes doesn't prove he wrote this one.
There's something I want to say.
When I first found your number, I thought maybe you were someone Daniel knew.
I was so worried about him that I didn't stop to think
how strange my message must have been for you.
I'm sorry I put you in that position.
And I do believe you when you say you didn't know my brother.
I haven't sent this whole file to the group.
Maya has enough on her mind.
And Lucas, well, you saw how that ended.
He wasn't wrong to worry about privacy.
There are other people's numbers in here,
and I don't want to expose them just because I'm desperate for answers.
If you're comfortable, I can make the export available to you privately after this call.
You could look at the start entry yourself and see what the file actually shows.
We can keep the other contacts masked in the viewer.
And if you'd rather not look at it right now, that's okay too.
I still have some of Daniel's old paper folders to go through.
I haven't checked those properly yet.
Whatever you decide, I won't share the whole contact list with the group.
I'll keep the copy safe.
You can look when you're ready, and if you notice anything,
we can talk about it without jumping to conclusions.
I'll keep looking through Daniel's things too.
Maybe there's something we've both missed.
Thank you for listening.
Really.
Talk soon.
Bye.
